# StreetVoxer

> StreetVoxer.net is a WebGPU browser game that renders the real world as interactive 3D voxels from satellite imagery, elevation data, and OpenStreetMap building footprints. You can walk, drive, fly, and shoot in a voxelized version of a real place. The site is scriptable end-to-end from a browser-automation agent (e.g. Claude-in-Chrome) via an in-page JavaScript API — no login, no repo access, and no server-side API required.

## How an agent drives the site

The full control surface is **in-page JavaScript on `window.debug`**, not an HTTP endpoint. **No browser? Three things still work:** read [`/agent-api.json`](https://www.streetvoxer.net/agent-api.json) for the documented surface in one GET, hand your user a **scenario link** (below) — a URL you can write by hand that opens the site and starts a game — or have the **MCP server** (below) write and check those links for you. With a browser you can run JS in, open the page, then:

- **Discover the API:** call `window.debug.api.list()` for every function as `{name, signature, documented}` (pass a substring or RegExp to filter, e.g. `window.debug.api.list(/^waitFor/)`), and read `window.debug.api.version` for the version (don't assume it). `window.debug.agentApiList()` is the same surface as annotated strings - signature plus usage notes and caveats - for the functions that have them. Both are live and are the source of truth; prefer them over any static doc, including this one, since the surface evolves.
- **Wait, don't poll.** The API is Promise-based. `await window.debug.waitForSpawn()` resolves when the player is controllable; `await window.debug.waitForChunksReady()` resolves when the voxel world around the player has finished building. Both reject with a structured `{reason,...}` on timeout.
- **Read state as structured data**, not by screenshotting: `getPlayerState()`, `getCharacterState()`, `getVehicleState()`, `getSurvival()`, `getQuestState()`.
- **Check the `reason` field on movement calls.** They resolve with `{reached, reason, ...}` rather than throwing, so a bee-line that failed looks like a success if you only await it.

Common entry points (call `api.list()` for the rest):

- `searchLocation(query)` / `waitForLocationSearchSpawn(query)` — geocode a place name and spawn there.
- `spawnAt({lat, lon, ctrl, elevMeters?, pitchDeg?, bearingDeg?})` — spawn at any coordinate in a chosen control mode, in-page, no reload.
- `setControlMode('FreeCamera' | 'Character' | 'Vehicle')` — switch modes at runtime.
- `walkCharacter(keys, ms)`, `walkCharacterToGeo({lat,lon}, opts?)`, `driveRoute(points)` — move a character headlessly (keys are UPPERCASE, e.g. `'W'`).
- `walkCharacterToPlace(target, opts?)` — use this, **not** `walkCharacterToGeo`, for anything inside a building: it walks to the door first. A bee-line at an indoor target walks into a wall.
- `moveFreeCameraTo({lat, lon, elevMeters?, bearingDeg?, pitchDeg?})`, `setCameraPitch(deg)`, `lookAtGeo({lat,lon})` — scripted free-camera framing (all angles in **degrees**).
- `spawnHelicopter()` / `enterHelicopter()` / `setHelicopterIntent(...)`, and the same trio for `Plane` — powered flight.
- `voxelEdit(op)` / `rapidVoxelEdit(op, n)` — edit voxels below the player (Character mode).

## MCP server

An MCP client can call StreetVoxer as tools, no browser needed: **`https://www.streetvoxer.net/api/mcp`** (Streamable HTTP, stateless, no auth). Tools: `coverage` (does a point have map data), `make_spawn_link` (a URL that opens a place), `make_scenario_link` (a URL that opens a place and starts a quest, checked by the game's own validator) and `read_scenario_link` (what a link does and whether the game accepts it). Every tool returns a link or an answer; nothing runs on the server, and a refused link comes back with the game's reason. Source, to run it locally over stdio: [StreetVoxer-Public](https://github.com/Cameron187/StreetVoxer-Public). Input schemas come from the server's `tools/list`; `/agent-api.json` lists the tools under `mcp`.

## URL / spawn contract

A spawn is fully described by the query string, which the page rewrites live every frame — so **any spawn URL is a shareable, replayable artifact** you can hand back to a user:

`https://www.streetvoxer.net/?lat=<deg>&lon=<deg>&bear=<deg>&ctrl=<0|1|2>&elev=<meters>&pitch=<deg>`

- `lat`, `lon` — WGS84 degrees. `bear` — camera bearing, degrees. `elev` — elevation, meters.
- `ctrl` — control mode: `0` FreeCamera, `1` Character, `2` Vehicle. **Only 0–2 are accepted on read.** The page can *emit* `ctrl=3`/`4` (helicopter / locked camera), so a copied URL may carry a mode that is silently ignored when reloaded — set those with `setControlMode` / `enterHelicopter` after load instead.
- `pitch` — camera pitch, degrees (0 level, −90 straight down); only lands on a FreeCamera (`ctrl=0`) spawn.
- `vehicle` — pick the vehicle spec before spawn: `humvee`, `motorcycle`, `boat`, `turret`. Unknown ids are ignored.
- `?clear-indexeddb` — drops the local cache before load (for a clean cold start).

## Scenario links — a game in a URL, no browser needed

Append a quest to any spawn URL, in the **fragment** (never sent to a server):

`https://www.streetvoxer.net/?lat=<deg>&lon=<deg>&bear=<deg>&ctrl=1#scenario=<encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({v:1, quest:<spec>, preload?:{radiusMeters}}))>`

`<spec>` is a `defineQuest` spec: `{id, name, reward?:{cents}, steps:[{verb, selector, at?, text?, ...}]}`. Useful verbs: `reached` / `drivenTo` (with selector `atGeo` and `at:{lat, lon, radiusMeters, name}`), `taken` (selector `spawnedVehicle`, `spawnParked:{specId:'humvee'}` parks a car beside the player), `edited` (selector `anyEdit`), `moved`, `firstPerson`. `{target}` in `text` is replaced with the target's name. When the user opens the link, the game spawns them at the pose and starts the quest; a malformed spec is refused **on screen with the reason**, and unknown fields are refused rather than ignored. Rules: `scope` must be `"once"` (the default); `reward.cents` at most 10000; keep the whole URL under ~2000 characters. Optional `preload:{radiusMeters, lat?, lon?}` (radius at most 1500 m, centre within 5 km of the spawn, default the spawn) generates and saves that area after spawn and before the quest starts, so the quest plays without load stalls; it takes a few minutes per km and the player can cancel it. `#scenario=b64.<base64url JSON>` is accepted too. The full format and a ready example are in `/agent-api.json` under `scenarioLinks`; with a browser, `window.debug.makeScenarioLink(spec)` builds and validates one.

## What to expect at a given place (read before "make a game at <place>")

The three data layers have **different coverage**, so "is it covered?" has three answers:

- **3D buildings — global.** OpenStreetMap-derived, eight archives, vintage **2026-09**. ⚠️ **Mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau are deliberately excluded** for compliance reasons (China's Surveying and Mapping Law mandates a coordinate offset this pipeline does not apply). Taiwan **is** covered. The exclusion boundary is coarse, so narrow strips of Mongolia, Russia, India and Vietnam within ~tens of km of the Chinese border are also missing. Everywhere else, including Antarctica, has buildings.
- **Ground imagery — high resolution in the US only.** Roughly 1 m/pixel across the United States. Elsewhere it is upscaled from a much coarser zoom (order 600 m per source pixel), so **non-US ground texture is heavily blurred** even though the buildings and terrain are correct. Set expectations accordingly: outside the US it looks like a correct city with soft ground, not a photo-real one.
- **Terrain elevation — global, quality varies.** ~30 m worldwide. Where a national elevation dataset was available the surface is clean; elsewhere it derives from older radar data and can show smooth mounds tens of metres high that are not real hills, particularly in dense cities.

Within building coverage, density is whatever OSM has: cities are dense, rural areas sparse — so "covered" means buildings exist, not that the view is urban. Requires a WebGPU-capable browser and a foreground (non-minimized) tab.

## Links

- [StreetVoxer.net](https://www.streetvoxer.net/): the live site — load it, then use `window.debug` as above.
- [StreetVoxer-Public on GitHub](https://github.com/Cameron187/StreetVoxer-Public): issues and feedback for the site, the agent kit (manifest, scenario-link codec, example scenarios) and the MCP server source.
- [Charleston, SC (dense 3D city, best-case imagery, Character mode)](https://www.streetvoxer.net/?lat=32.776&lon=-79.931&ctrl=1): example US spawn — buildings, terrain and ~1 m imagery all at their best.
- [London (dense 3D city outside the US)](https://www.streetvoxer.net/?lat=51.5074&lon=-0.1278&ctrl=1): example non-US spawn — full buildings and clean terrain, blurred ground imagery.
